paper.title: Regret Analysis of the Anytime Optimally Confident UCB Algorithm

settings.name_in_paper: Finite-horizon stochastic multi-armed bandit with Gaussian rewards N(mu_i,1)
settings.definition_quote: In each round the learner chooses an arm $I_t \in \set{1,\ldots,d}$ based on past observations and receives a Gaussian reward $X_t \sim \mathcal N(\mu_{I_t}, 1)$ where $\mu \in \R^d$ is the vector of unknown means. ... $R^\pi_\mu(n) = \E\left[\sum_{t=1}^n (\mu^* - \mu_{I_t})\right]$

algorithms.name: Gittins strategy with flat Gaussian prior (Algorithm 1)
Finite-horizon Gittins index strategy with Gaussian prior

source.label: thm:finite
source.quote: Let $\pi$ be the strategy given in \cref{alg:flat}. Then there exist universal constants $c, c' > 0$ such that $R^\pi_\mu(n) \leq c \sum_{i: \Delta_i > 0} \left(\frac{\log(n)}{\Delta_i} + \Delta_i \right)$ and $R^\pi_\mu(n) \leq c' \left(\sqrt{dn \log(n)} + \sum_{i=1}^d \Delta_i\right)$

results.notes: Universal unspecified constant c, recorded as O. d is number of arms (K). The appendix claims, without a formal statement, that the same bounds hold for the fully Bayesian strategy when d=2 and for the approximate Gittins index. Compute: the index is computed by a lookup table in O(n^2 N) time; marked polynomial with some uncertainty. Metadata title differs from the paper source (Gittins index paper).

source.label: thm:finite
source.quote: Then there exist universal constants $c, c' > 0$ such that ... $R^\pi_\mu(n) \leq c' \left(\sqrt{dn \log(n)} + \sum_{i=1}^d \Delta_i\right)$

results.notes: Problem-independent bound; the constant c' is universal.

tuning: Gaussian prior with prior variances sigma_i^2 > 0 for all arms (arbitrary prior means)

source.label: thm:asymptotic
source.quote: Assume that $\sigma_i^2 > 0$ for all $i$. Let $\pi_n$ be the strategy given in \cref{eq:nonflat}, then there exists a universal $c > 0$ such that for $\mu \in \R^d$, \, $\limsup_{n\to\infty} R^{\pi_n}_\mu(n) / \log n \leq c \sum_{i : \Delta_i > 0} \Delta_i^{-1}$.

results.notes: Frequentist regret for a fixed mean vector; the limit is over a sequence of horizon-dependent strategies. The prior is an algorithm input, not an assumption on the instance.
